list.detail: You were still braking at 74% with 96° of steering. Braking moves weight to the front, so the rear has little grip while you turn.

list.detail: A wheel was on a kerb or the grass just before the slide, which takes grip away suddenly.
list.fix: Stay off the kerbs in this corner (or use less of them), especially while on the throttle.

list.detail: You were 7 km/h faster here than on your best lap, more than the tyres could hold.
list.fix: Brake a little earlier or harder into this corner.

list.detail: You ran out of road without a clear slide beforehand, usually a too-early turn-in or a slightly wide line.
list.fix: Turn in a little later and aim for the apex; see the line columns in the steering table.

list.detail: You were braking at 49% while turning 450°. Tyres can't brake hard and steer hard at the same time.
list.fix: Release the brake progressively as you turn in so the front tyres have grip left for steering.

findings.title: T2: 22 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T3: 16 m of coasting
findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T1: slow to build brake pressure (1.01 s)
findings.detail: Get to peak pressure in about 0.1-0.2 s. The car has the most grip when it is fastest, so the first part of the braking zone is where to brake hardest.

findings.title: T2: slow to build brake pressure (1.29 s)
findings.detail: Get to peak pressure in about 0.1-0.2 s. The car has the most grip when it is fastest, so the first part of the braking zone is where to brake hardest.

findings.title: T3: slow to build brake pressure (1.05 s)
findings.detail: Get to peak pressure in about 0.1-0.2 s. The car has the most grip when it is fastest, so the first part of the braking zone is where to brake hardest.

findings.title: T2: you usually turn in 37 m later than on your best lap
findings.detail: Pick a fixed turn-in marker (a board, kerb start or shadow) and use it every lap.

setup.title: No consistent balance problem detected
setup.detail: Handling looks reasonably neutral from the data. Focus on driving technique first.

setup.title: FR: middle cooler than edges
setup.detail: Pressure is too low. Raise it ~0.5-1 psi.

setup.title: RL: inside only 1.8°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RR: inside only -4.1°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: Fronts running 17.6°C hotter
setup.detail: Fronts are overworked, which is a sign of understeer / sliding the front. Matches the balance notes above if understeer was detected.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 2 of 3 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T2, T3. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 3 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 83.1% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

pros.title: Very few locked wheels
pros.detail: You are not flat-spotting tyres under braking.

pros.title: Consistent through T2
pros.detail: Your section times there barely change from pass to pass, so you have found a repeatable approach.

pros.title: Your fastest passes through T3 were slower at the apex
pros.detail: That's "slow in, fast out" working: giving up a little apex speed for a better exit. Do it every lap in these corners.

cons.title: Coasting: 8.6% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 38 m per lap in T2, T3. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Slow to build brake pressure (T1, T2, T3)
cons.detail: It takes you 1.01 s / 1.29 s / 1.05 s to reach peak. Aim for 0.1-0.2 s.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T1, T3
cons.detail: T1: 0.94 s between your average and best pass; T3: 0.17 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T2, T3.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T1, T3: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Shows trail braking and throttle overlap at a glance. Optional once your technique is consistent.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Let AMS2 set steering lock for each car, and watch the FFB meter for clipping.

traits.name: Speed
traits.text: Quick. Braking points come up fast.

traits.name: Cornering grip
traits.text: Modest grip, like a sporty road car.

traits.name: Braking power
traits.text: Weak brakes: brake early and carry momentum instead.

traits.name: Wheelspin tendency
traits.text: The engine can't overpower the tyres: full throttle is almost always safe.

traits.name: Downforce
traits.text: No downforce: grip is the same at any speed.

traits.name: How forgiving
traits.text: Forgiving; a good car to learn in.

tips: Low grip: brake in a straight line, turn smoothly, and avoid sudden inputs.
